text: Your whole shoulder, with one pulley and a cable row triangle.
No dumbbells, and no waiting for a machine.
Four exercises that hit the front, the side, and the rear.
Three sets of twelve, each.
Your shoulder is three pieces.
And most people train only the front one, mostly with the press.
One: the lateral raise.
Pulley low, grab one side of the triangle, and lift your arm to shoulder height.
The cable pulls from below, so the shoulder works from the very first centimetre.
Two: face pull.
Pulley at eye level, both hands, and elbows out wide.
Three: front raise, with both hands, up to eye level.
Four: stand side-on to the pulley, pulley low, arm across the front, then open it out behind you.
Front, side, and rear.
And your mate who only presses? Still doing half a shoulder.
Now picture the next twelve weeks.
Train all three heads a couple of times a week, and the shoulder starts to fill out.
Week four: the caps start to round out.
Week eight: you can see the width from the front.
Week twelve: broader shoulders, and a proper V-taper.
Everyone grows at a different rate, but steady progress is what drives it.
So, which head have you been missing?
